source.description:
PROBLEM
'xt pi <name> --bead <id>' writes the beads claim kv under the LAUNCHING session's id, not the launched session's. Observed twice on 2026-09-08 launching lanes for unitAI-rrdnt.47 and unitAI-rrdnt.20 from coordinator session 088c856b-5b68-4b1d-a44a-7c3ecc8d9367:

  claimed:088c856b-...(the coordinator)  = unitAI-rrdnt.47
  claimed:01a07e4a-...(the launched pi)  = unitAI-rrdnt.47

Both exist. The launched session's claim is correct; the coordinator's is spurious.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is not cosmetic. The commit gate refuses the COORDINATOR's next commit with 'Close open issues before committing — Claimed: <the lane's bead> (still in_progress)'. The coordinator is then told to close a bead another session is actively working on, and the only correct action — clearing a kv key by hand — is not one the error suggests. A coordinator that dispatches lanes and merges their work is exactly the session that cannot afford a false claim.

Both launches also printed 'bead assignee: pi did not signal readiness within 30s; session launch continues', and the assignee stayed on the shared actor rather than becoming pi/<slug>. The two symptoms are likely the same handshake failing: the readiness signal that would carry the launched session's identity never arrives, and something falls back to the caller's identity instead of failing.

SCOPE
The xt pi --bead claim/assignee handshake. CROSS-REPO: xtrm-tools, not this repo.

WORKAROUND used twice today: bd kv clear "claimed:<launcher-session-id>" after launch, and bd update <bead> --assignee pi/<slug>.

TBD
Whether the 30s readiness timeout is the root cause or a second symptom.
source.title: xt pi --bead stamps the claim under the LAUNCHING session, blocking the launcher's own commits
